matches.note: R6 notes deletion never voids pending changes, but says the harm is applying them after a re-subscribe, not that applyPendingChanges re-grants a paid tier on a CANCELLED row.
Same defect: no payment_behavior, so an incomplete subscription still has the paid tier persisted and synced.
Both say resolvePlayerTierKey and the marketplace projection read the stored tier without any status gate.
Same defect: downgrade and applyPendingChanges never update the Stripe price, so billing stays at the old tier.
No report says changeCoachTier/changePlayerTier skip the status check.
R10 catches that grace expiry is local-only and Stripe keeps billing, but wrongly says re-subscribe is blocked; in fact the CANCELLED row passes the guard and a second Stripe subscription is created.
Same stale pastDueSince that gives zero grace on a later payment failure.
R11 covers the missing event-ordering guard and R2 mentions UNPAID normalisation, but neither raises the CHECK violation and webhook retry loop, or the missing invoice.paid handler.
Same defect: stale detached entity saved after the Stripe call with no @Version.
R1 explicitly flags the customer+price key replaying a stale subscription within 24h.
R2 notes the local tier is upgraded before the proration is collected, but not the deferral mechanism of CREATE_PRORATIONS or the upgrade-then-cancel loss.

unmatched_reported.note: Challenges the deliberate Decision 3 swallowing of PessimisticLockingFailureException, which the answer key lists as a non-finding.
Concrete trigger: a lowercase tier makes valueOf throw after Stripe has created the subscription, which rolls back the local row.
Concrete trigger: SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1 in the void query can miss a pending downgrade the scheduler has locked, so the downgrade is later applied.
Concrete trigger: choosing the same tier goes down the downgrade branch, voiding the real pending change and inserting an X→X change.
Concrete trigger: an update webhook arriving before the local persist is acknowledged and lost, so the status transition is dropped.
Low-impact alert-accuracy speculation about the orphan grace window.
Concrete trigger: a coach who also pays for a child's player subscription gets a false orphan alert from the sweep every day.
Speculative; the reporter itself says it is safe if the listener is AFTER_COMMIT.
Concrete race: two concurrent subscribes for different tiers have different idempotency keys, so both create Stripe subscriptions and one is left billing unlinked.
The price fields are filled from the priceId config key, so clients see Stripe ids instead of amounts.
Comment and alert-noise speculation that depends on unverified registration code.
